name: Sergey Ioffe
blurb: Co-inventor of Batch Normalization (2015), a layer that made training very deep convolutional networks far faster and more stable.

name: Christian Szegedy
blurb: Co-inventor of Batch Normalization and a key architect of Google's deep vision systems (Inception, ResNet-class networks).

name: Boris Teodorovich Polyak
blurb: Soviet mathematician who introduced the heavy-ball/momentum method (1962), letting optimizers carry velocity through flat regions.

name: ResNet (Residual Network)
blurb: He et al.'s skip-connection architecture that let gradients flow through hundreds of layers, making very deep CNNs trainable.

name: Highway Network
blurb: Srivastava, Greff & Schmidhuber's learnable-gating skip connections, the precursor to ResNet, seven months before it.

name: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)
blurb: Piecewise-linear activation max(0,x) that prevents vanishing gradients and makes deep networks trainable; standard workhorse of CNNs.

name: GELU (Gaussian Error Linear Unit)
blurb: Hendrycks & Gimpel's smooth activation that became the standard in Transformer feed-forward blocks (GPT-style models).

name: SiLU / Swish
blurb: Self-gated activation x*sigmoid(x) found by Google's search; used in Stable Diffusion's U-Net ResBlocks and modern vision stacks.

name: Softmax
blurb: Bridle's function turning logits into a probability distribution; the standard output layer for multi-class classification.

name: Neocognitron
blurb: Fukushima's hierarchical pattern-recognition network, one of the first CNNs and the first use of a ReLU-like activation.

name: Perceptron
blurb: Rosenblatt's single-layer model with a Heaviside output; the founding neural-network architecture of modern deep learning.

name: VGG (VGGNet)
blurb: Simonyan & Zisserman's deep 3x3-convolution CNN from Oxford; a plain-network baseline that ResNet overcame.

name: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
loc: Yorktown Heights, New York, United States
blurb: LeCun's IBM architecture using shared-weight convolutional layers; the backbone of nearly all computer-vision models.

name: Backpropagation
blurb: The 1986 Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams algorithm (first in Werbos's thesis) that trains networks by propagating error backward.

name: Gradient Descent
blurb: Cauchy's method of stepping against the gradient to minimize a function; the fundamental optimization rule behind training.

name: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
loc: New York, New York, United States
blurb: Robbins-Monro stochastic approximation applied to optimization; the base optimizer whose mini-batch noise shapes what nets find.

name: Momentum (SGD)
blurb: Polyak's heavy-ball method that adds a velocity term to accumulate past gradients and power through flat regions.

name: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation)
blurb: Kingma & Ba's per-parameter adaptive optimizer; the default for training most modern neural networks and large language models.

name: Batch Normalization (BatchNorm)
blurb: Ioffe & Szegedy's layer that rescales activations per batch, enabling higher learning rates and faster convergence of deep nets.

name: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm)
blurb: Ba et al.'s batch-independent normalization that is the stability glue inside every Transformer (GPT) block.

name: Group Normalization (GroupNorm)
blurb: Wu & He's batch-size-independent channel-group normalization; the default in Stable Diffusion's U-Net at batch size 1.

name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
blurb: Dosovitskiy et al.'s application of the Transformer to image patches; replaced CNNs as a top vision architecture.

name: GPT
blurb: OpenAI's family of large Transformer language models (GPT-3, GPT-4) trained on next-token prediction.

name: Transformer
blurb: Vaswani et al.'s attention-based architecture that replaced recurrence and underlies all modern large language models.

name: U-Net
blurb: Ronneberger et al.'s encoder-decoder network for image segmentation; the denoiser backbone of Stable Diffusion.

name: DeepDream
blurb: Google's gradient-based image stylization tool; already used jitter to cancel the deconvolution checkerboard artifact.

name: Stable Diffusion
blurb: A latent U-Net diffusion model for image generation; its ResBlocks use Conv → GroupNorm → SiLU.

name: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
blurb: Hu et al.'s parameter-efficient fine-tuning that trains tiny low-rank weight updates instead of the whole model.

name: QLoRA
blurb: Dettmers et al.'s 4-bit quantized LoRA that fine-tunes a 70B model on a single consumer GPU.

name: Adapter Modules
blurb: Houlsby et al.'s small bottleneck layers inserted between Transformer blocks for parameter-efficient transfer learning.

name: Prompt Tuning
blurb: Lester et al.'s method of learning continuous soft prompts prepended to inputs, freezing the base model.

name: IA³ (Layer-Scaling)
blurb: Liu et al.'s few-shot method learning only scaling vectors on attention and feed-forward weights.

name: DoRA (Weight-Decomposed LoRA)
blurb: Liu et al.'s decomposed magnitude-and-direction low-rank adaptation that often beats LoRA at the same rank.

name: PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
blurb: The policy-gradient method behind RLHF; used in the InstructGPT pipeline to align models with human feedback.

name: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)
blurb: OpenAI's post-training pipeline (reward model + PPO) that shaped ChatGPT's helpful, aligned behavior.

name: InstructGPT
blurb: Ouyang et al.'s first large model aligned by instruction fine-tuning plus RLHF; the direct ancestor of ChatGPT.

name: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
blurb: Rafailov et al.'s closed-form preference optimizer that matches PPO without a separate reward model or rollouts.

name: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)
blurb: DeepSeek's critic-free reasoning optimizer; the method behind DeepSeek-R1's emergent long chain-of-thought.

name: Dropout
blurb: Srivastava et al.'s regularization that randomly zeroes inputs during training, forcing robust redundant representations.

name: Lasso (L1 Regularization)
blurb: Tibshirani's L1 penalty that drives unimportant weights to exactly zero, performing automatic feature selection.

name: Ridge Regression (L2 Regularization)
blurb: Hoerl & Kennard's L2 weight penalty (descended from Tikhonov's) that shrinks weights toward zero for smoother fits.

name: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM)
blurb: Foret et al.'s optimizer that penalizes loss sharpness by descending from a nearby perturbation, improving generalization.

name: Saddle-Free Newton
blurb: Dauphin et al.'s second-order method that ignores negative Hessian eigenvalues to escape saddle points in deep nets.

name: Hopfield Network
loc: Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States
blurb: Hopfield's attractor network that used a physical spin system's energy as the loss; a precursor to modern retrieval networks.

name: Chinchilla
blurb: DeepMind's 70B model and Hoffmann et al.'s compute-optimal scaling law tying loss to parameters and training tokens.

name: MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding)
blurb: Hendrycks et al.'s 57-subject multiple-choice benchmark for measuring a language model's breadth of knowledge.

name: HumanEval
blurb: OpenAI's benchmark of 164 hand-written programming problems used to measure a model's code-generation ability.

name: Goodhart's Law
blurb: Goodhart's observation that a measure which becomes a target becomes a bad measure; central to AI evaluation failure.

name: Heaviside Step Function
blurb: The 0/1 activation of the original Perceptron; differentiable nowhere, which blocked gradient-based training.

name: ResNet wins ImageNet (ILSVRC) 2015
blurb: December 2015: ResNet took the ImageNet classification competition, proving residual connections made depth practical.

name: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
blurb: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber's gated recurrent unit whose gates solve vanishing gradients over time; the standard sequence-memory cell.

name: CIFAR-10
blurb: Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton's 60,000-image benchmark of 10 classes; the default testbed for deep-vision and loss-landscape studies.
